The panel talks to your servers exclusively through the Cipi REST API. Before installing it, make sure each server you want to manage has the API enabled with a token that covers the full ability set. $ cipi api api.example.com $ cipi gui panel.example.com Each managed server needs cipi api installed and a Bearer token with all abilities. See the API setup guide to generate one; since Cipi 5.9.0 , cipi api token create --name=gui --full-access creates a token that has every ability, including the ones later releases add. A running Cipi server (Ubuntu 24.04 / 26.04) to host the panel — this can be one of the servers you manage or a small dedicated box. A domain or subdomain of its own , pointed at that server with a DNS A (and AAAA ) record, e.g. panel.example.com . The panel is a separate Laravel application with its own Nginx vhost and certificate. It cannot share a hostname with an app, or with the API, which needs its own too, e.g. api.example.com (see a domain of its own ). Since Cipi 5.7.0 , Cipi refuses a domain that is already taken. cipi api enabled on every server you want to control, each with a full-ability token (include www-manage , status-view , and for app tooling apps-env , apps-auth , apps-artisan , apps-run , apps-deploy-config ). For Node apps, redirects and proxies, managed servers need API 1.31+ and Cipi 5.4.1+ (the 5.4.1 migration opens those commands to the panel sudoers); the deploy audit needs Cipi 5.4.0+ . Server → Disk needs API 1.33+ , the disk-view ability and Cipi 5.5.2+ (migration 5.5.2). The app's cipi.yml tab needs API 1.35+ , the yml-view /

One command provisions the whole panel on a Cipi server: a dedicated PHP-FPM pool, an Nginx vhost for your domain, and a scheduler cron job. The Laravel app is bundled at /opt/cipi/gui , the same model used by the cipi-api package. Since Cipi 5.8.2 the command checks the DNS first — the domain must already point at the server, or it stops with the record to create ( --skip-dns-check behind a NAT or proxy it cannot see through) — and ends with the Let's Encrypt certificate ( --no-ssl to skip it). cipi gui panel.example.com The installer prompts interactively for the first administrator account — an email and a password. The password must satisfy the panel's policy: Minimum 12 characters . At least one uppercase, one lowercase, one digit, and one special character. No more than 4 identical consecutive characters. Configuration is written to /etc/cipi/gui.json . Once the command finishes, open your domain in a browser and log in with the admin account you just created. The domain you pass is the panel's alone. If you have an app on example.com on the same server, the panel goes on a subdomain such as panel.example.com , not on example.com or one of the app's aliases. Cipi refuses those, and refuses the API's domain. Picked the wrong one? cipi gui move changes it. cipi gui <domain> issues the certificate itself (Cipi 5.8.2+). Before that, or after --no-ssl , the panel is served over plain HTTP until you run cipi gui ssl .

Issue (or re-issue) a free Let's Encrypt certificate for the panel's domain and switch it to HTTPS. cipi gui <domain> does this itself since Cipi 5.8.2; the command stays for a certificate skipped with --no-ssl or one that failed. It checks first that the domain points at the server ( --skip-dns-check to go ahead anyway). The panel is HTTPS-aware and sets the correct forwarded headers behind the Cipi Nginx vhost. cipi gui ssl The certificate renews automatically through the same ACME renewal that Cipi uses for app domains. Since 5.7.0 a failed certbot run is reported as a failure (exit 1). Before, the command could print “SSL installed” anyway.

Moves the panel to a new domain or subdomain. Admin accounts, 2FA enrolments and saved server connections stay; admins sign in again, since their sessions belong to the old domain. cipi gui move panel.newdomain.com # move and issue the new certificate cipi gui move panel.newdomain.com --no-ssl # move now, certificate later (cipi gui ssl) Point the new domain at the server first (DNS A / AAAA record). The Nginx vhost is rewritten for the new domain. If nginx -t rejects it, the old vhost goes back and nothing else changes. /etc/cipi/gui.json and APP_URL are updated. SSL: the old domain's certificate is deleted, so nothing keeps renewing it, and one is issued for the new domain. If that fails, the panel is already on the new domain over HTTP: fix DNS or port 80 and run cipi gui ssl . The managed servers need no change: the panel calls their API URLs, and their IP whitelists are by IP, not by domain. To move a managed server's API instead, run cipi api move on that server and update its URL under Connections. Cloudflare Zero Trust: a panel routed through the tunnel is tied to its hostname (DNS record, tunnel route, Access app). Run cipi zt hostname remove --gui before the move, then cipi zt hostname add --gui and cipi zt access enable --gui after it. cipi gui move refuses to run until the hostname is off the tunnel.

The panel uses classic session login and supports optional TOTP two-factor authentication . Each administrator can enrol an authenticator app (Google Authenticator, 1Password, Aegis, …) from their profile. 2FA is opt-in per user, not forced. With single sign-on the identity provider is the authority for MFA: the TOTP step is skipped after an SSO sign-in and kept for password sign-ins. If an administrator loses access to their second factor, an operator with shell access can clear it from the server with cipi gui reset-user , which rewrites the account and removes the 2FA enrolment.

d: Sign in with Entra ID, Google or any OpenID Connect provider.
x: Since Cipi 5.8.2 and cipi/gui 4.0.2 the panel can sign people in through your identity provider over OpenID Connect : Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace, Okta, Keycloak, Authentik — anything that publishes a discovery document ( /.well-known/openid-configuration ). SAML is not supported. SSO is opt-in and configured from the server , because the panel's .env is Cipi's file to write; the same place is the break-glass when a provider is misconfigured. 1. Register the panel at your identity provider Create an OIDC client (a “web application”) and give it the panel's callback as the redirect URI

h: 1. Register the panel at your identity provider
x: Create an OIDC client (a “web application”) and give it the panel's callback as the redirect URI: https://<panel-domain>/auth/sso/callback . You will get back a client id and a client secret; note the issuer URL too. Microsoft Entra ID — Entra admin center → App registrations → New registration: single-tenant, platform Web , redirect URI as above. Then Certificates & secrets → New client secret. The issuer is tenant-specific : https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant-id>/v2.0 (the Directory (tenant) ID from the Overview page, never common or organizations : the panel compares the issuer of every token with the one you configured). Users need a mail address on their account; the email claim is read from the userinfo endpoint. Google Workspace — Google Cloud console → APIs & Services → Credentials → OAuth client ID, type Web application , authorised redirect URI as above. Issuer: https://accounts.google.com . Restrict who can sign in with --domains . Okta, Keycloak, Authentik, Zitadel, Auth0 — a standard OIDC web client with the authorization-code flow (PKCE is used, a client secret is still required). The issuer is the realm or application URL whose /.well-known/openid-configuration answers.

h: 2. Turn it on from the server
x: cipi gui sso set --issuer=https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant-id>/v2.0 \ --client-id=<application-id> --client-secret=<secret> # Entra ID; the secret is asked when omitted cipi gui sso set --issuer=https://accounts.google.com --client-id=… --client-secret=… --domains=example.com cipi gui sso status # issuer, label, Redirect URI, who can get in, SSO-only or not cipi gui sso only on # password sign-in off for everyone — the SSO button only cipi gui sso only off # break-glass: passwords accepted again cipi gui sso disable # back to password sign-in; accounts and their links are kept set writes the settings to the panel's .env , clears the config cache, runs the pending migration and prints the Redirect URI to check against the one registered at the provider. The login page gets a Sign in with … button, labelled after the issuer (“Microsoft Entra ID”, “Google”, “Okta”, else “SSO”; --label= to change it). Flags: Flag What it does --issuer=<url> The OIDC issuer; its discovery document is fetched and cached for an hour. Required, https:// only. --client-id=<id> The client (application) id from the provider. Required. --client-secret=<secret> The client secret. Asked on the terminal when omitted; kept when you re-run set to change another flag. --label=<text> The button text instead of the one derived from the issuer. --domains=<a.com,b.com> Email domains whose people get an account on their first sign-in : role user , no access until an admin grants servers or apps in Team. Without it only existing accounts can sign in. --only Password sign-in off for everyone, the same as c

Existing accounts — seeded by cipi gui , created from an invite link — are matched by their email (case-insensitive) and linked to the provider's identity ( users.sso_subject ) on the first sign-in; from then on the link wins, so a renamed mailbox still lands on the same account. An email already linked to a different identity is refused (“linked to another identity”). New people get an account only when their email domain is in --domains ; everyone else sees “No panel account for … Ask an admin for an invite link.” Nothing is created for a refused sign-in. Roles and grants are the panel's, as before: an auto-created account is a user with nothing granted; admins hand out servers and apps in Team, where SSO-linked accounts carry an SSO badge. MFA: the identity provider is the authority — the panel's own TOTP step is skipped after an SSO sign-in. Password sign-ins keep their TOTP as before. Under the hood: authorization-code flow with PKCE (S256), state and nonce ; the code is exchanged server-to-server with the client secret; the identity comes from the provider's userinfo endpoint , and the ID token's issuer, audience and nonce are checked against the handshake. An email_verified: false claim is refused; a provider that does not send the claim (Entra ID) is accepted. Where it shows: Settings → Panel has a read-only Single sign-on card for admins (status, provider, SSO-only, auto-provisioned domains, the redirect URI to copy, and the CLI to change it); the panel's own .env keys are CIPI_GUI_SSO_ISSUER , _CLIENT_ID , _CLIENT_SECRET , _LABEL , _DOMAINS , _ONLY , _SCOPES .

h: 4. Changing provider, locking yourself out, and other troubles
x: A new issuer or client id (another tenant, a new app registration) makes set forget every link: an identity's sub is per provider, and Entra ID's is per app registration. Everyone links again at the next sign-in by email; nothing else changes. SSO-only and a broken provider: from the server, cipi gui sso only off brings password sign-in back, cipi gui sso disable turns SSO off altogether, cipi gui reset-user resets the admin account. Nothing in the panel can bypass SSO-only, by design. “redirect_uri mismatch” from the provider: the URI registered there differs from the one cipi gui sso status prints (scheme, host, trailing path). After cipi gui move register the new one. “issuer mismatch” : Entra ID configured with common or organizations instead of the tenant id, or an issuer with a trailing path the provider does not put in its tokens — use the exact issuer value from the discovery document. “no email claim” : the account has no mail address, or the client was not granted the email scope (Entra: API permissions → Microsoft Graph → email , openid , profile ). preferred_username is not accepted as an email. Every cipi gui sso change is logged in cipi.log and raises the gui_sso notification trigger (Security).

Two commands cover the common cases: cipi gui update — soft update Runs composer update cipi/gui , applies database migrations, and refreshes the compiled theme. This is the day-to-day update path. cipi gui update cipi gui upgrade — full rebuild Rebuilds the panel from scratch. Use it after a major release, or if an environment has drifted and a clean reinstall of the app code is the fastest way back to a known-good state. cipi gui upgrade cipi gui re

h: Updating — gui update vs gui upgrade
x: The panel ships as the cipi/gui Composer package, so updates are ordinary Composer updates plus migrations. Two commands cover the common cases:
Runs composer update cipi/gui , applies database migrations, and refreshes the compiled theme. This is the day-to-day update path. cipi gui update
Rebuilds the panel from scratch. Use it after a major release, or if an environment has drifted and a clean reinstall of the app code is the fastest way back to a known-good state. cipi gui upgrade
Recompiles and reloads the panel theme without touching code or the database — handy after a theme tweak. cipi gui refresh-theme
Report the panel's current status — whether it is installed, its domain, and the health of its services. cipi gui status

Repair the panel's PHP-FPM open_basedir restriction and all runtime file permissions. Run it if the panel starts throwing permission or autoload errors after an update — including the HTTP 500 after cipi gui upgrade / soft update fixed in 5.0.18 (Composer symlink for cipi/gui outside open_basedir ). cipi gui fix-permissions

Rewrite an administrator's email, name and password, and clear their 2FA enrolment — the recovery path when someone is locked out. reset-password is an alias for the same command. Locked out by SSO-only or a broken provider? cipi gui sso only off brings password sign-in back first. cipi gui reset-user

h: Removing the panel — cipi gui remove
x: Uninstall the panel: its Nginx vhost, PHP-FPM pool, scheduler, application, config and the Let's Encrypt certificate of its domain. A certificate that an app still uses is kept. Your servers and apps are untouched, since the panel is only a client of the API. uninstall is an alias, and --force skips the confirmation prompt. A panel on the Cloudflare tunnel must come off it first ( cipi zt hostname remove --gui ). cipi gui remove cipi gui remove --force Removing the panel is the ultimate expression of its optionality: uninstall it any time and Cipi is back to a pure CLI, exactly as it was before. The API on each server stays; remove it separately with cipi api remove if nothing else uses it.

Soft disk limits and Cloudflare DNS accounts have been on the API since 1.32 (the PHP SDK calls them); the panel shows the limit and points at cipi app limits and cipi ssl dns on the host to change them. cipi ssh apps and cipi firewall attempts stay on the host CLI. d: Install the API, create tokens and call every endpoint.
x: Cipi can optionally enable a REST API layer on the server via cipi api <domain> . It is powered by the Laravel package cipi/api (current release 1.34.0 . node_build on app create and repository_access in the job results need Cipi 5.6.0+ ; disk usage needs Cipi 5.5.2+ so the API sudoers allow cipi disk ; soft disk limits and Cloudflare DNS-01 accounts need 5.5.0+ , and http / wildcard: false on SSL install need 5.5.1+ . Redirects, proxies and Node restart still need 5.4.1+ ), which exposes: $ cipi api api.example.com $ cipi api token create --name=ci --abilities=apps-view,deploy-manage $ curl -

The API is not installed inside an app. It is a separate Laravel application with its own Nginx vhost and its own certificate, so it needs a domain or subdomain that only the API uses . Pick a subdomain such as api.example.com and create a DNS A record (and AAAA for IPv6) that points it at the server, before you run cipi api <domain> : since 5.8.2 the command checks the DNS first and stops, with the record to create, when the name does not resolve or points elsewhere (the Cloudflare proxy counts as pointing here; --skip-dns-check behind a NAT or proxy it cannot see through). It then installs the API, issues the Let's Encrypt certificate ( --no-ssl to skip) and, on a terminal, offers to create the first token ( --no-token to skip). cipi api ssl and cipi api move run the same DNS check. What Example domain Set up with Your app example.com , www.example.com cipi app create , cipi alias add Panel API + MCP api.example.com cipi api api.example.com Control panel (GUI) panel.example.com cipi gui panel.example.com The three can live on the same server and under the same registered domain: what matters is that each hostname belongs to one of them only. Since Cipi 5.7.0 , Cipi refuses any overlap. cipi api and cipi api move will not take the domain or an alias of an app, or the GUI's domain. In the other direction, cipi app create , cipi app edit --domain , cipi alias add , cipi app clone , cipi sync import and cipi.yml aliases will not take the API's or the GUI's domain. API on an app's domain (before 5.7.0): Nginx ends up with two vhosts with the same server_name , serves only one

On a normal Cipi server you never install the package manually — cipi api <domain> provisions Laravel at /opt/cipi/api , Nginx, SSL, SQLite job queue, and cipi-queue.service . For reference or custom setups: composer require cipi/api php artisan vendor:publish --tag=cipi-config php artisan vendor:publish --tag=cipi-assets php artisan migrate php artisan cipi:seed-api-user php artisan cipi:token-create Panel .env uses CIPI_APPS_JSON=/etc/cipi/apps.json (or apps-public.json projection for non-sensitive fields). Token abilities are defined in config/cipi.php — list them with php artisan cipi:token-abilities (same list as cipi api token create since Cipi 4.6.3 ). Source and changelog: github.com/cipi-sh/api (MIT). Client wrappers: cipi-cli and the PHP SDK ( cipi/sdk ).

cipi api <domain> # DNS check, install, certificate, token — one command (--no-ssl --no-token --skip-dns-check) cipi api ssl # (re)issue the Let's Encrypt certificate (--skip-dns-check) cipi api move <domain> # move to another domain: old certificate out, new one in cipi api remove # uninstall API + MCP, tokens, vhost, crons and certificate cipi api token list # list tokens cipi api token create # create a new token (choose abilities) cipi api token create --name=ci --full-access # v5.9.0+ a token that may do everything cipi api token create --name=ci --abilities=apps-view,deploy-manage --expires=2027-06-30 cipi api token revoke <id> # revoke a token cipi api status # Laravel + cipi-api versions, queue worker, pending jobs, FPM pool cipi api fix-permissions # repair panel storage/database ownership (www-data) cipi api update # soft update: composer update on Laravel and API packages cipi api upgrade # full rebuild with rollback at /opt/cipi/api.old

h: Changing the API domain — cipi api move
x: Installed the API on the wrong domain, or rebranding? Move it. The Laravel app, tokens, job history and IP whitelist stay exactly as they are; only the address changes. cipi api move api.newdomain.com # move and issue the new certificate cipi api move api.newdomain.com --no-ssl # move now, certificate later (cipi api ssl) Point the new domain at the server first (DNS A / AAAA record): Let's Encrypt checks it over port 80. cipi api move rewrites the Nginx vhost for the new domain. If nginx -t rejects it, the old vhost goes back and nothing else changes. It updates /etc/cipi/api.json and APP_URL , and restarts cipi-queue . SSL: it deletes the old domain's certificate, including any -0001 copies certbot made, so nothing renews a domain the server no longer serves. Then it issues a certificate for the new domain. If that fails (DNS not propagated yet, port 80 closed), the API is already on the new domain over HTTP: fix the cause and run cipi api ssl . A certificate that an app still uses is never deleted. Then update the URL in every client of the server: the server's entry in the GUI (Connections), the cipi-cli profile, the PHP SDK configuration and MCP clients ( https://api.newdomain.com/mcp ). Tokens keep working. Running cipi api <other-domain> on a server whose API is already configured stops and points you to cipi api move . Before 5.7.0 it silently changed domain, lost the HTTPS configuration and left the old certificate renewing.

h: Removing the API — cipi api remove
x: Uninstalls everything cipi api <domain> set up. Your apps, databases and the GUI are untouched. uninstall is an alias, and --force skips the confirmation. cipi api remove cipi api remove --force It removes: the cipi-queue worker the Nginx vhost and the PHP-FPM pool the scheduler, maintenance and nightly update crons the Let's Encrypt certificate of the API domain /opt/cipi/api , /opt/cipi/api.old and the upgrade backups api.json , the IP whitelist and the API logs All tokens die with it, so GUI panels, cipi-cli and MCP clients that use this server lose access. The www-data sudoers whitelist ( /etc/sudoers.d/cipi-api ) stays, because it is part of every Cipi install. Reinstall any time with cipi api <domain> : you get a new, empty token database.

After cipi self-update , root-owned files under /opt/cipi/api or /opt/cipi/gui can prevent PHP-FPM ( www-data ) from writing logs or the SQLite job database — the browser shows a bare HTTP 500 on /docs or /mcp . Cipi normally repairs ownership automatically during self-update (migration 5.0.13+ reclaims API/GUI ownership); if problems persist: cipi api fix-permissions # chown storage, database, bootstrap/cache, .env → www-data cipi api status # confirm Laravel version, queue worker, pending jobs The panel's Backups tab says "not configured" on a server where backups run. The tab shows what cipi backup status --json answers when the API runs it. Compare on the server, as root: ls -l /etc/cipi/backup.json # the file `cipi backup configure` writes sudo -u www-data sudo -n /usr/local/bin/cipi backup status --json | head -c 300 # exactly what the panel runs No file: backups were configured on another server, or never with cipi backup configure . "configured": true from the second command: the server is fine and the answer is lost on the way — panel 4.2.1 and API 1.39.1 show the error instead of "not configured" ( cipi api update , cipi gui update ). sudo asking for a password: /etc/sudoers.d/cipi-api does not list the backup commands — the migration of Cipi 5.9.0 writes them. cipi api status prints the installed Laravel and cipi/api package versions, whether cipi-queue.service is active, pending async jobs in the panel SQLite database, and PHP-FPM pool stats for the API vhost (including slow requests when configured). cipi api update soft-updates the panel API package from Packa

Authentication uses Sanctum . Each token can have one or more abilities that limit allowed operations: apps-view — read apps apps-create — create apps apps-edit — edit apps (PHP, repository, branch, primary domain since API 1.9.0+ / Cipi 4.6.2+ ) apps-suspend — suspend and unsuspend apps apps-basicauth — enable, disable, and inspect HTTP Basic Auth on apps (API 1.10.0+ ) apps-env — list/merge app .env keys (API 1.14.0+ / Cipi 5.0.3+ ) apps-auth — manage shared Composer auth.json (API 1.14.0+ ; distinct from apps-basicauth ) apps-artisan — run Artisan as an async job (API 1.14.0+ ) apps-run — whitelisted non-interactive app run (API 1.14.0+ ) apps-deploy-config — structured Deployer recipe options (API 1.14.0+ ) php-view — list installed PHP versions (API 1.15.0+ ) php-manage — install PHP versions (API 1.15.0+ ; install-only since 1.19.0 — removing a version or switching the default stays on the CLI) ssh-view — list SSH keys on the cipi user (API 1.15.0+ ) ssh-manage — add/remove/rename SSH keys (API 1.15.0+ ) services-view — list system services (API 1.15.0+ ) services-manage — restart services (API 1.15.0+ ) smtp-view — read SMTP notification settings (password never returned; API 1.15.0+ ) smtp-manage — configure, enable, disable, test, delete SMTP (API 1.15.0+ ) health-view — list healthchecks (API 1.15.0+ ) health-manage — set, unset, and run healthchecks per app (API 1.15.0+ ) ip-whitelist-view — read panel API / MCP IP allowlist (API 1.15.0+ ) ip-whitelist-manage — edit IP allowlist entries (API 1.15.0+ ) redirects-view / redirects-manage — read and change whole-app

All endpoints require the Authorization: Bearer <token> header. Write operations (create, edit, delete, deploy, rollback, unlock, SSL, alias, www, database) are asynchronous: they return 202 Accepted with a job_id to poll via GET /api/jobs/{id} — with the ability the job was created under ( apps-create for an app create, dbs-manage for a database password, …; API 1.36.1+ — before, any token could read any job by id). Read-only endpoints such as GET /api/dbs , GET /api/dbs/engines , GET /api/status , GET /api/apps/{name}/www , and GET /api/apps/{name}/logs (API 1.11.9+ ), GET /api/php , GET /api/ssh/keys , GET /api/services , GET /api/smtp , GET /api/health , GET /api/ip-whitelist (API 1.15.0+ / Cipi 5.0.6+ ), and the API 1.31.0 additions — redirects, proxies, GET /api/node , the deploy audit, search, packages, monitor and Zero Trust — are synchronous. Since API 1.32.0 , GET /api/apps/{name}/limits and GET|PUT|DELETE /api/ssl/dns are synchronous too ( PUT on limits is the async job app-limits ). Since API 1.33.0 , GET /api/disk and GET /api/disk/dbs are synchronous and measured on request. Since API 1.35.0 , GET /api/apps/{name}/yml and POST /api/apps/{name}/yml/auto/enable|disable are synchronous; POST /api/apps/{name}/yml/apply is the async job app-yml-apply . POST /api/apps accepts optional custom (boolean) and docroot (string) parameters for creating custom apps with classic deployment. The repository field is required for Laravel apps and optional for custom apps: omit it (or send empty) to provision an SFTP-only site aligned with Cipi v4.5.1+ . When no repository is se

Omit octane for classic PHP-FPM. Use "engine": "pgsql" when PostgreSQL is installed (API 1.12.0+ / Cipi 4.8+ ). The panel API runs as www-data and executes Cipi CLI commands via sudo using /etc/sudoers.d/cipi-api — an explicit whitelist of cipi subcommands. Vault and MariaDB credentials stay inside Cipi, not in PHP. GET /api/dbs — runs sudo cipi db list (sync). Requires Cipi 4.4.17+ (migration adds cipi db … to sudoers). Without it: sudo: a terminal is required . Multi-engine list/engines need Cipi 4.8+ / API 1.12.0+ . GET /api/status / MCP ServerStatus — prefer sudo cipi status (API 1.11.8+ ); host-read fallback when sudo fails (includes postgresql since API 1.12.1+ ). MCP ServiceList — sudo cipi service list MCP AppArtisan — sudo cipi app artisan <app> … Since Cipi 5.0.6+ / API 1.15+ : php list|install|remove|switch , ssh list|add|remove , service list|restart , status , db install|default|engines , app webhook recreate , smtp status|configure|enable|disable|test|delete , api ip-whitelist (+ args) in the sudoers whitelist (migration 5.0.6 creates the default IP whitelist file and regenerates /etc/sudoers.d/cipi-api on cipi self-update ). Since Cipi 5.0.3+ / API 1.14+ : app env , app artisan , app run , auth create|edit|show|delete , and deploy-config in the sudoers whitelist (migration regenerates /etc/sudoers.d/cipi-api on cipi self-update ). Since Cipi 5.2.2+ : search status|list|enable|disable and package list in the sudoers whitelist. search install|upgrade|key rotate|remove and package install|remove stay off it — they change or destroy server state and stay with the operator on the CLI. Since Cipi 5.2.3+ : the manual stack upgrades — nginx upgrade , db upgrade and service upg

Since Cipi 5.0.6+ , restrict panel API and MCP clients by source IP. Default file /etc/cipi/api-ip-whitelist is * (allow all). One IPv4/IPv6 address or CIDR per line (or comma-separated --ips= ). cipi api ip-whitelist show cipi api ip-whitelist add 203.0.113.10 cipi api ip-whitelist set --ips=203.0.113.0/24,2001:db8::/32 cipi api ip-whitelist allow-all cipi api ip-whitelist show --json REST equivalents live under /api/ip-whitelist (API 1.15.0+ ). PUT auto-adds the caller IP when tightening the list unless ensure_client_ip: false .

Interactive documentation is available at /docs (Swagger UI). The OpenAPI spec is generated from public/api-docs/openapi.json and covers apps (including suspend, unsuspend, domain rename, basic auth, .env , Composer auth.json , Artisan / app-run jobs, deploy-config, fix-permissions, paginated logs, www redirects, Octane and Node create, and multi-engine engine ), app and path redirects, proxies, Node runtimes, aliases, deploy and deploy audit, SSL (install + force HTTPS), databases (engines list + optional engine on mutations), search, packages, monitor, Zero Trust, server status, job polling with structured result types, and MCP tool schemas. Current API package version: 1.34.0 (1.30.0 was published in error from an old commit — skip it). 1.32.0 adds app type , /api/apps/{name}/limits and /api/ssl/dns . 1.33.0 adds /api/disk and /api/disk/dbs . 1.34.0 adds node_build to POST /api/apps (the Laravel asset build, same rule as the CLI) and repository_access to the app-create result, and to the app-edit result when the repository or branch changed: status ( ok , nobranch , denied ), branch , error and the CLI fix as hint . 1.35.0 adds /api/apps/{name}/yml , …/yml/apply and …/yml/auto/enable|disable with the yml-view / yml-manage abilities (Cipi 5.6.4+ ).

An MCP (Model Context Protocol) server is exposed at /mcp via Streamable HTTP. Since API package 1.11.1+ , a token with the mcp-access ability is sufficient for all MCP tools — per-endpoint REST abilities ( apps-view , deploy-manage , apps-basicauth , www-manage , etc.) are not checked on /mcp . The server exposes 73 tools (one tools/list page; MCP server 1.3.0) for app, alias, www, redirects, proxies, Node, database, deploy and deploy audit, SSL, HTTP Basic Auth, search, limits, disk usage, cipi.yml , server management (PHP, SSH, services, SMTP, health, IP whitelist, packages, monitor, Zero Trust), .env / auth.json / app-run / deploy-config, job polling, logs, Artisan, and server monitoring. Write operations that dispatch async jobs return a job_id — poll with JobShow (API 1.11.0+ ). Basic auth actions and read-only tools run synchronously. Applications: AppList , AppShow , AppCreate (optional engine , octane ), AppEdit , AppSuspend , AppUnsuspend , AppDelete , AppDeploy , AppDeployRollback , AppDeployUnlock , AppArtisan (Laravel apps only; rejects custom apps and tinker ), AppEnvShow , AppEnvUpdate , AppAuthJson* , AppRun , AppRunCommands , AppDeployConfigShow , AppDeployConfigUpdate , AppWebhookRecreate (API 1.15.0+ / Cipi 5.0.6+ ; earlier app tooling requires API 1.14.0+ / Cipi 5.0.3+ ), AppFixPermissions (API 1.31.0+ ), AppLimitsShow , AppLimitsUpdate (API 1.32.0+ ; disk_limit_gb needs Cipi 5.5.0+ ), AppYmlShow , AppYmlApply (async job), AppYmlAuto ( app , enabled ) — the app's cipi.yml (API 1.35.0+ / Cipi 5.6.4+ ) Redirects & proxies: RedirectList , RedirectSet , Redi

The MCP endpoint is optional and loads only when the required MCP package is installed. To use it from VS Code , Cursor , or Claude Desktop : Configure the API with cipi api <domain> and cipi api ssl Create a token with cipi api token create and select at least mcp-access Add the MCP server to your client config (see below) Cursor Add to ~/.cursor/mcp.json (or Cursor → Settings → MCP): { "mcpServers": { "cipi-api": { "type": "http", "url": "https://<your-api-domain>/mcp", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer <your-token>" } } } } Cursor connects natively over HTTP — no bridge needed. cipi-cli is a standalone Go binary that talks to the Cipi REST API from your local machine. No SSH required — manage apps, deployments, SSL, databases (including anonymized dumps), PHP versions, services, SSH keys, SMTP, healthchecks and disk usage from any terminal. Binaries are available for Linux and macOS (amd64 and arm64). $ cipi-cli api token add prod $ cipi-cli status $ cipi-cli staging deploy myapp The Cipi server must have the API package installed and configured before using cipi-cli . See cipi api for setup instructions.
Download the latest release for your platform from the Releases page , then: chmod +x cipi-cli-* sudo mv cipi-cli-* /usr/local/bin/cipi-cli
git clone https://github.com/cipi-sh/cli.git cd cli make build sudo make install
cipi-cli version cipi-cli v1.6.0 (linux/amd64)

A profile is a named connection to one Cipi server (API endpoint + token). Use as many profiles as you have servers — for example prod , staging , or client-a . You need the API endpoint URL and a Sanctum token created with cipi api token create on each server. Credentials are stored per profile in ~/.cipi/config.json with permissions 0600 . Always pass a profile name — if you omit it, the CLI prompts for one instead of silently writing to default .

Recommended: store the token with api token add . Equivalent helpers are configure --profile and profiles add : cipi-cli api token add prod Cipi API endpoint: https://api.example.com API token: 1|yourtoken... Server profile "prod" saved → ~/.cipi/config.json cipi-cli api token add staging Cipi API endpoint: https://staging-api.example.com API token: 1|stagingtoken... Server profile "staging" saved → ~/.cipi/config.json # Same flow via configure / profiles add cipi-cli configure --profile prod cipi-cli profiles add staging
cipi-cli api token add prod \ --endpoint https://api.example.com --token "1|yourtoken..." cipi-cli profiles add staging \ --endpoint https://staging.example.com --token "1|yourtoken..."
cipi-cli profiles show prod Profile: prod Endpoint: https://api.example.com Token: 1|a8Kz...4f2a cipi-cli profiles show # Shows all configured server profiles

Manage multiple server connections from a single cipi-cli installation. One profile equals one server. Prefix any command with a profile name to target that server, or set a default with profiles use to omit the prefix. The aliases servers / server work the same as profiles .

cipi-cli prod apps list cipi-cli staging apps show myapp cipi-cli prod deploy myapp cipi-cli prod ssl install myapp With a default server set, you can run commands without the prefix: cipi-cli profiles use prod Default profile set to "prod" cipi-cli apps list # Uses the prod profile cipi-cli staging apps list # Explicit prefix still targets staging Command Description cipi-cli api token add [profile] Add or update API endpoint + token for a named server profile cipi-cli profiles List configured servers (alias: cipi-cli servers ) cipi-cli profiles add [name] [flags] Add or update a server profile (same as configure --profile ) cipi-cli profiles list List configured servers cipi-cli profiles show [profile] Show one server profile, or all if omitted cipi-cli profiles use <profile> Set the default server (alias: profiles default ) cipi-cli profiles delete <profile> [-y] Delete a local server profile (credentials only — nothing changes on the remote server) api token add , profiles add , and configure accept the same flags: --endpoint and --token (plus --profile when the name is not positional). Aliases: servers / server → profiles ; profiles use → profiles default . The same management commands are also available under cipi-cli configure list , configure show , configure default , and configure delete — prefer profiles or api token add for storing credentials.

Manage applications on your Cipi server. Command Description cipi-cli apps list List all applications cipi-cli apps show <name> Show application details — the environment label included (cipi-cli 1.9.0+, Cipi 5.8.0+) cipi-cli apps create [flags] Create a new application cipi-cli apps edit <name> [flags] Edit an application cipi-cli apps delete <name> [-y] Delete an application cipi-cli apps suspend <name> Take an app offline (HTTP 503 maintenance page) without deleting it cipi-cli apps unsuspend <name> Restore a suspended app to normal service cipi-cli apps logs <name> [flags] Read paginated application logs (nginx, PHP-FPM, Laravel, worker, deploy) cipi-cli apps fix-permissions <name> Restore the app home permissions (Cipi 5.2.1+) cipi-cli apps artisan <name> [command...] Run an Artisan command as an async job (Cipi 5.0.3+) cipi-cli apps run <name> [command...] Run a whitelisted app binary — see cipi-cli run-commands (Cipi 5.0.3+) cipi-cli apps env show|set <name> Read .env , or merge keys with --set KEY=VALUE / --unset KEY (Cipi 5.0.3+) cipi-cli apps auth show|create|update|delete <name> Manage the shared Composer auth.json (Cipi 5.0.3+) cipi-cli apps basicauth status|enable|disable <name> HTTP Basic Auth in front of the app ( --user , --password ; auto-generated when omitted) cipi-cli apps node status|restart <name> Node app status and blue-green restart (Cipi 5.4.0+) cipi-cli apps search enable|disable <name> Meilisearch / Laravel Scout for one app (Cipi 5.2.2+) cipi-cli apps webhook recreate <name> [--rotate-secret] Recreate the Git deploy webhook, optionally rotating

--user Application name (used as Linux user and database name) --domain Primary domain for the application --php PHP version (e.g. 8.5 ) --repository Git repository URL --branch Git branch to deploy from --env Environment label, e.g. production (default) or staging — lowercase letters, digits, - , _ , max 32 characters (cipi-cli 1.9.0+, API 1.36+, Cipi 5.8.0+). Written to the app's .env as APP_ENV / CIPI_ENV and picks the cipi-<env>.yml the app reads before cipi.yml --custom Create a custom (non-Laravel) app with htdocs deploy --docroot Document root relative to htdocs (custom apps only) --engine Database engine: mariadb or pgsql (Cipi 4.8+) --octane Laravel Octane mode: true , false or frankenphp (Cipi 5.0+) --node Create a Node app: spa , static or ssr (Cipi 5.4.0+). A repository is required and --php is not accepted --framework Node framework preset: next , nuxt , sveltekit , astro , remix or vite --node-version Node major version (e.g. 22 or 24 ) --build Node build command --start Node start command (SSR apps) --output Node build output directory (spa / static apps) --health-path Node health path checked during blue-green restarts (SSR apps)

--php Change PHP version --repository Update Git repository URL --branch Change deploy branch --env Change the environment label (cipi-cli 1.9.0+, Cipi 5.8.0+); same as cipi app edit --env --domain Rename the primary domain (requires Cipi 4.6.2+ and API 1.9.0+ ) --node … --node , --node-version , --build , --start , --output , --health-path — update the Node app settings listed under create flags

--type Log type filter: all (default), nginx , php , worker , deploy , or laravel --page Page number, starting at 1 for the most recent lines (default 1 ) --per-page Lines per log file per page (default 50 , max 1000 ; requires API 1.11.9+ )

# List all apps cipi-cli apps list # Create a Laravel app cipi-cli apps create --user=myapp --domain=myapp.com \ --php=8.5 --repository=git@github.com:acme/myapp.git --branch=main \ --node-build= 'npm ci && npm run build' # asset build on every deploy (1.7.0+) # A staging app of the same repository (cipi-cli 1.9.0+, Cipi 5.8.0+): reads cipi-staging.yml before cipi.yml cipi-cli apps create --user=myapp-stg --domain=staging.myapp.com \ --repository=git@github.com:acme/myapp.git --branch=develop --env=staging # Create a custom (non-Laravel) app cipi-cli apps create --user=landing --domain=landing.acme.com \ --custom --docroot=dist # Edit an existing app cipi-cli apps edit myapp --php=8.4 # Suspend staging for maintenance cipi-cli apps suspend staging # Read recent deploy logs (page 1 = newest lines) cipi-cli apps logs myapp --type=deploy # Paginate older nginx lines cipi-cli apps logs myapp --type=nginx --page=2 --per-page=100 # Run Artisan, read and update .env cipi-cli apps artisan myapp migrate --force cipi-cli apps env show myapp cipi-cli apps env set myapp --set APP_DEBUG=false --unset OLD_KEY # Create a Node SSR app cipi-cli apps create --user=web --domain=web.acme.com --node=ssr --framework=next \ --repository=git@github.com:acme/web.git --branch=main # Recreate the Git webhook with a new secret cipi-cli apps webhook recreate myapp --rotate-secret # Delete an app (skip confirmation) cipi-cli apps delete myapp -y Since 1.7.0 (Cipi 5.6.0 , API 1.34+ ), apps create prints the app's credentials, deploy key and build when the job finishes, and both apps create and apps edit

List every primary domain and alias across all apps on the server in a single table — the remote counterpart to cipi domains on the server. Useful for auditing DNS coverage or spotting domains missing SSL before a certificate renewal. Command Description cipi-cli domains List every domain and alias across all apps cipi-cli domains DOMAIN APP KIND TYPE PHP SSL api.myapp.com myapp alias Laravel 8.5 ✓ myapp.com myapp primary Laravel 8.5 ✓ www.myapp.com myapp alias Laravel 8.5 ✓ 3 domains · 1 app · 3 certificates The global domain map is built from GET /api/apps on the server. It requires Cipi 4.5.5+ on the server (for the underlying cipi domains data) but no minimum API package version.

Trigger deployments, rollback to the previous release, or unlock a stuck deployment. Command Description cipi-cli deploy <app> Trigger a zero-downtime deployment cipi-cli deploy rollback <app> [-y] Rollback to previous release cipi-cli deploy unlock <app> Unlock a stuck deployment cipi-cli deploy config show|set <app> Read or update structured deploy.php options (Cipi 5.0.3+) cipi-cli deploy audit <app> [--days N] Deploy audit ledger: origin, operator, IP and commit of every deploy (Cipi 5.4.0+) cipi-cli yml <app> The app's cipi.yml : file, validity, auto-apply and what applying would change (Cipi 5.6.4+); the environment and the cipi-<env>.yml in use (cipi-cli 1.9.0+, Cipi 5.8.0+) cipi-cli yml apply <app> Apply the committed cipi.yml as an async job (Cipi 5.6.4+) cipi-cli yml auto <app> on|off|status Apply cipi.yml after every successful deploy, or stop (Cipi 5.6.4+) deploy config set flags: --keep-releases N , --migrate , --optimize , --storage-link , --queue-restart , --horizon-terminate , --predeploy-snapshot , --node-build CMD and --extra-artisan CMD (repeatable). The remote counterparts of cipi deploy-config and the deploy audit ledger . The yml commands are the remote side of cipi yml plan | apply | auto . They need API 1.35+ , Cipi 5.6.4+ and a token with yml-view (read) and yml-manage (apply, auto). A token created before 1.35 has neither, so expect a 403 until you issue a new one. Turning auto-apply on asks for confirmation: from then on, anyone who can push to the repository can change the app's server settings. cipi-cli deploy myapp Deploying myapp... Polling jo

Install Let's Encrypt certificates for your applications. Command Description cipi-cli ssl install <app> Install Let's Encrypt certificate (covers primary domain and all aliases) cipi-cli ssl force <app> Re-apply the HTTP → HTTPS redirect (Cipi 4.8+) cipi-cli ssl install myapp Certificate provisioned for myapp.com

Manage the www ↔ apex counterpart of an app — the remote side of cipi www . DNS for the domain (and its aliases) must already point to the server. Requires Cipi 4.8+ (API 1.12+) and the www-manage ability. Command Description cipi-cli www status <app> Show the www / apex redirect status cipi-cli www add <app> Add the www or apex counterpart as an alias cipi-cli www force-to-root <app> 301 redirect www → apex cipi-cli www force-from-root <app> 301 redirect apex → www cipi-cli www clear <app> Remove the canonical www redirect # Add www.myapp.com and make it canonical cipi-cli www add myapp cipi-cli www force-from-root myapp cipi-cli www status myapp

Whole-app and path redirects, plus prefix reverse proxies — the remote side of cipi redirect and cipi proxy . Requires Cipi 5.4.1+ (API sudoers, API 1.31+) and the redirects-view|manage / proxies-view|manage abilities. Aliases: redirects → redirect , proxy → proxies . Command Description cipi-cli redirect list <app> List the whole-app redirect and every path redirect cipi-cli redirect set <app> --to URL [--code 301] [--keep-path] Redirect the whole app to a URL (one hop; path and query kept unless --keep-path=false ) cipi-cli redirect enable|disable <app> Toggle the whole-app redirect without removing it cipi-cli redirect unset <app> Remove the whole-app redirect cipi-cli redirect add <app> --from /path --to URL [--code] [--keep-path] Add a path redirect — a trailing slash on --from means prefix match cipi-cli redirect remove <app> --from /path Remove a path redirect cipi-cli proxies list <app> List prefix reverse proxies cipi-cli proxies add <app> --prefix /api --upstream URL [flags] Proxy a path prefix to an upstream ( --strip-prefix , --preserve-host , --timeout 60 , --buffering ) cipi-cli proxies remove <app> --prefix /api Remove a prefix proxy # Send the old blog to the new one, keep paths cipi-cli redirect add myapp --from /blog/ --to https://blog.acme.com/ # Proxy /api to an internal service cipi-cli proxies add myapp --prefix /api --upstream http://127.0.0.1:8080 --strip-prefix cipi-cli proxies list myapp

Manage domain aliases for an application. Command Description cipi-cli aliases list <app> List all aliases for an app cipi-cli aliases add <app> <domain> Add a domain alias cipi-cli aliases remove <app> <domain> [-y] Remove a domain alias cipi-cli aliases add myapp www.myapp.com Alias www.myapp.com added to myapp. cipi-cli aliases list myapp www.myapp.com api.myapp.com # Re-run ssl install to include new aliases in the certificate cipi-cli ssl install myapp

Manage MariaDB and PostgreSQL databases on the server, and request anonymized dumps from Laravel apps that run cipi/agent . Aliases: database , dbs → db . Command Description cipi-cli db engines List installed database engines and the server default (Cipi 4.8+) cipi-cli db install <engine> Install an engine: mariadb or pgsql (Cipi 5.0.6+) cipi-cli db list [--engine E] List databases with their size, optionally filtered by engine cipi-cli db create <name> [--engine E] Create a database (MariaDB unless --engine pgsql ) cipi-cli db delete <name> [-y] Delete a database — API < 1.19 only; newer servers use cipi db delete on the host cipi-cli db backup <name> Create a compressed backup on the server cipi-cli db restore <name> [-y] Restore the latest backup (overwrites current data) cipi-cli db password <name> [-y] Regenerate the password and update the linked app .env cipi-cli db anonymize <app> --email <addr> Request an anonymized dump of the app database via cipi/agent (cipi-cli 1.5.0+) cipi-cli db anonymize download <url> [-o file] Download the dump from the signed link received by email cipi-cli db list NAME SIZE myapp 24.5 MB blog 8.2 MB cipi-cli db backup myapp Backup created: myapp_20260402_143022.sql.gz cipi-cli db restore myapp -y Database restored successfully.

The anonymizer is not part of the Cipi API: it lives in the cipi/agent package inside the Laravel app. The CLI reads the app URL ( APP_URL , else https://<primary domain> ) and CIPI_ANONYMIZER_TOKEN from the app .env through the API ( apps-view + apps-env abilities), then calls POST /<CIPI_ROUTE_PREFIX>/db on the app itself. The agent runs the job in the app queue and emails a signed download link valid for 15 minutes. # One-time setup on the app (all through the Cipi API) cipi-cli apps artisan myapp cipi:service anonymize --enable cipi-cli apps artisan myapp cipi:generate-token anonymize cipi-cli apps artisan myapp cipi:init-anonymize # then edit /home/myapp/.db/anonymization.json on the server # Request a dump — the signed link arrives by email cipi-cli prod db anonymize myapp --email dev@example.com ✓ Anonymization job queued for 'myapp' # Download it: default name from the server, -o - streams to stdout cipi-cli db anonymize download "https://myapp.com/cipi/db/<token>?expires=…&signature=…" -o myapp.sql cipi-cli db anonymize download "<signed url>" -o - | mysql -u root myapp_local --email, -e Address that receives the signed download link (prompted when omitted) --url Override the app base URL, e.g. when the app redirects to www — redirects are never followed --token Override the bearer token read from .env --output, -o download : output file ( - for stdout) --force, -f download : overwrite an existing file Requires cipi-cli 1.5.0+ , Cipi 5.0.3+ / API 1.14+ (for apps env ) and cipi/agent 1.1.1+ with the anonymizer enabled in the app. Custom and Node apps are refused. Installed PHP versions and PHP-FPM status — the remote side of cipi php . Requires Cipi 5.0.6+ (API 1.15+) and the php-view / php-manage abilities. Switching the default version and removing versions stay host-only ( cipi php switch|remove ). Legacy versions (7.4–8.2 on a server installed before Cipi 4.5.4) are listed and marked (legacy) ; no app can be created on or moved to one. Command Description cipi-cli php list Installed versions, FPM status and the server default cipi-cli php install <version> Install PHP 8.3 , 8.4 , 8.5 or 8.6 (async job; 8.6 needs Cipi 5.9.1+ / API 1.39.2+) cipi-cli php list cipi-cli prod php install 8.5

System services and the authorized SSH keys of the cipi user — the remote side of cipi service and cipi ssh . Requires Cipi 5.0.6+ (API 1.15+) with services-view|manage and ssh-view|manage . Aliases: service → services , ssh → ssh-keys . Command Description cipi-cli services list [name] System services and their status, or one service cipi-cli services restart <name> Restart a service ( nginx , mariadb , php8.5-fpm , …) cipi-cli ssh-keys list Authorized keys of the cipi user, with ids cipi-cli ssh-keys add [key] [--file F] Add a public key, inline or from a .pub file cipi-cli ssh-keys remove <id> [-y] Remove a key by id cipi-cli services list cipi-cli services restart nginx cipi-cli ssh-keys add --file ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub cipi-cli ssh-keys list

Configure the outgoing email the server uses for notifications — the remote side of email notifications . The stored password is never shown. Requires Cipi 5.0.7+ (API 1.15+) and smtp-view|manage . Command Description cipi-cli smtp show Current SMTP configuration cipi-cli smtp set [flags] Create or update the configuration; omitted flags keep the stored values cipi-cli smtp test Send a test email cipi-cli smtp enable|disable Toggle notifications cipi-cli smtp delete [-y] Remove the configuration

--host SMTP host --port SMTP port (default 587 ) --user SMTP username --password SMTP password — required the first time; omit to keep the stored one --from Sender address --to Notification recipient --tls Use STARTTLS / TLS (default on) --enabled Enable notifications after saving (default on) --no-test Do not send a test email after saving cipi-cli smtp set --host smtp.example.com --port 587 --user notify@example.com \ --password "s3cret" --from notify@example.com --to ops@example.com cipi-cli smtp test

HTTP healthchecks per app — the remote side of cipi health . Requires Cipi 5.0.7+ (API 1.15+) and health-view|manage . Command Description cipi-cli health list All configured app healthchecks and their state cipi-cli health show <app> One app's healthcheck and last result cipi-cli health set <app> [--url] [--expect] Enable or update the check cipi-cli health unset <app> Disable the check cipi-cli health check <app> Run the check now; exits 1 when unhealthy Without --url , https://<primary domain>/up is checked (wildcard-domain apps need an explicit URL). --expect is the HTTP status considered healthy (default 200 ). The exit code of health check makes it usable as a CI gate. cipi-cli health set myapp --url https://myapp.com/up --expect 200 cipi-cli health check myapp cipi-cli health list

Restrict which client IPs may call the panel API (default * = allow all). Requires Cipi 5.0.8+ (API 1.15+) and ip-whitelist-view|manage . Command Description cipi-cli ip-whitelist show Show the API client IP allowlist cipi-cli ip-whitelist set <entries...> Replace the whitelist ( * = allow all) cipi-cli ip-whitelist add|remove <ip> Add or remove one IP / CIDR cipi-cli ip-whitelist allow-all Reset to * When restricting, the IP you are calling from is kept in the list so you do not lock yourself out. Pass --no-ensure-client-ip to set to skip that safety net. cipi-cli ip-whitelist set 203.0.113.10 198.51.100.0/24 cipi-cli ip-whitelist show

Read-only views of host features, each mirroring its cipi counterpart on the server and needing the matching *-view ability. All support --json . Command Description cipi-cli search status Meilisearch status (Cipi 5.2.2+) cipi-cli node list Installed Node runtimes (Cipi 5.4.0+) cipi-cli monitor System monitor checks and state (Cipi 5.3.0+) cipi-cli packages Optional host packages catalog (Cipi 5.2.2+) cipi-cli zt Cloudflare Zero Trust status (Cipi 5.3.0+) cipi-cli run-commands Whitelisted binaries accepted by apps run (Cipi 5.0.3+) cipi-cli prod monitor cipi-cli node list --json

Read the same host snapshot as cipi status on the server — via GET /api/status . Bare status shows a global overview (one row per configured server). Pass a profile name (or use a profile prefix) for full details. Command Description cipi-cli status Global overview — one row per server (alias: status all ) cipi-cli status <profile> Full details for one server cipi-cli <profile> status Same detail view, via profile prefix Global columns: NAME , IP , CPU , RAM , HDD , APPS , SVC , CIPI . The default profile is marked with * . cipi-cli status NAME IP CPU RAM HDD APPS SVC CIPI prod* 203.0.113.10 12% 48% (3840M) 42G/80G 53% 3 8/8 ok 4.6.3 staging 203.0.113.20 4% 31% (2048M) 18G/40G 45% 1 8/8 ok 4.6.3 * default profile Detail: cipi-cli status <name> cipi-cli status prod Server status — prod Endpoint https://api.example.com Hostname prod-01 IP 203.0.113.10 OS Ubuntu 24.04 Uptime 12 days Cipi 4.6.3 CPU 12% RAM 3840/8192 MB (48%) HDD 42G/80G (53%) Apps 3 Requires the API token ability status-view and GET /api/status on the server (API 1.11.6+ ). Create or rotate the token with cipi api token create and include status-view .

Who is filling the disk — the same figures as cipi disk on the host, read from GET /api/disk and GET /api/disk/dbs . An app is its home (releases, shared storage, logs) plus its database, largest first. The server measures sizes when asked, so the CLI waits up to three minutes. Requires cipi-cli 1.6.0+ , Cipi 5.5.2+ (API sudoers; the host command exists since 5.5.0), API 1.33+ and the disk-view ability. Command Description cipi-cli disk The filesystem /home is on, then every app (GB and %) cipi-cli disk db Every database per engine, in MB (aliases: dbs , databases ) cipi-cli disk --json The same figures for scripts ( disk db --json too) cipi-cli <profile> disk Same reading, on one server cipi-cli disk cipi-cli prod disk db cipi-cli disk --json Server disk MOUNT SIZE USED FREE USE / 100.00 GB 40.00 GB 60.00 GB 40% Apps (3) — % of the 100.00 GB on / APP FILES DATABASE TOTAL DISK LIMIT shop 2.00 GB 1.00 GB 3.00 GB 3.0% 10 GB (30%) blog 0.50 GB 120.4 MB 0.62 GB 0.6% — front 0.10 GB 0.00 GB 0.10 GB 0.1% — All apps 3.72 GB 3.7% Everything else 36.28 GB 36.3% FILES is the app home. DATABASE is the database named after the app and, when shared/.env points DB_DATABASE at another one, that one too. TOTAL is both; DISK is that total as a percentage of the filesystem. LIMIT is the soft limit set on the host with cipi app limits <app> --disk=<GB> — alerts only, nothing is blocked — and reads over once passed, — when the app has none. Everything else is the rest of the used space: system, packages, logs, local backups, databases that belong to no app. Sizes below 0.01 GB are printed in M

h: disk db — every database, in MB
x: MariaDB and PostgreSQL report one size per database. Valkey only knows how many keys each logical database holds, and Meilisearch how many documents each index has: for those two the size is the engine's, in memory and on disk. An engine that is not installed is left out. How each engine is measured is on the host command . MariaDB — sizes in MB DATABASE SIZE blog 2.0 MB shop 200.0 MB On disk 500.0 MB (whole engine) Valkey — sizes in MB DATABASE KEYS SIZE db0 1204 — Memory in use 12.3 MB On disk 3.0 MB (whole engine) Requires the API token ability disk-view . A token created before API 1.33 does not have it — run cipi api token create on the host and include disk-view . HTTP 503, or terminal is required , means the server is older than Cipi 5.5.2 : cipi self-update so the API sudoers allow cipi disk .

Write operations (create, edit, delete, deploy, SSL, etc.) are asynchronous on the Cipi API. The CLI automatically polls for job completion and displays a spinner while waiting. If you prefer to handle polling manually, use the jobs commands. Command Description cipi-cli jobs show <id> Show job status cipi-cli jobs wait <id> Wait for a job to complete (blocking) cipi-cli jobs show 42 Job #42: deploy myapp — completed cipi-cli jobs wait 43 Waiting for job #43... completed

Update cipi-cli to the newest release from GitHub. The command picks the highest semver among published releases (not GitHub’s “latest” flag, which can point at an older tag), downloads the matching binary for your platform, verifies its SHA-256 checksum, and replaces the running binary in place. Aliases: self-update , upgrade . Command Description cipi-cli update Update to the highest published semver cipi-cli update --force Reinstall even if already up to date (allows downgrade) cipi-cli update Downloading cipi-cli v1.6.0... Checksum verified. Updated to v1.6.0. # Aliases work the same cipi-cli self-update cipi-cli upgrade # If installed in a system path, use sudo sudo cipi-cli update

Install shell autocompletion for cipi-cli . The recommended path is completion install , which detects your shell, writes the completion script, and hooks it into your rc file (idempotent). Command Description cipi-cli completion install Auto-detect shell and install completion cipi-cli completion install --shell zsh Install for a specific shell ( zsh , bash , or fish ) cipi-cli completion zsh Print the zsh completion script to stdout cipi-cli completion bash Print the bash completion script to stdout cipi-cli completion fish Print the fish completion script to stdout cipi-cli completion install Installing zsh completion... Completion installed → ~/.cipi/completions/cipi-cli.zsh Hooked into ~/.zshrc # Or pin a shell explicitly cipi-cli completion install --shell bash For zsh and bash, the script is written under ~/.cipi/completions/ and a source line is appended to your shell rc file. For fish, the script goes to ~/.config/fish/completions/ (auto-loaded). Reload the shell afterwards, then try cipi-cli <TAB> .

These flags are available on all commands. --json Output in JSON format — useful for scripting and CI/CD pipelines --no-color Disable colored output --help Show help for any command # JSON output for scripting cipi-cli apps list --json [{"name":"myapp","domain":"myapp.com","php":"8.5"}, ...] # Pipe to jq for filtering cipi-cli apps list --json | jq '.[].name' "myapp" "blog" # Help for a specific command cipi-cli apps create --help
Releases are automated via GitHub Actions. Pre-built binaries for Linux (amd64/arm64) and macOS (amd64/arm64) are published with SHA-256 checksums on the GitHub Releases page .
cipi-cli is open source, MIT licensed, and written in Go. Contributions welcome on GitHub .

The Cipi server must have the API package installed and configured before using cipi-cli : cipi api <domain> cipi api ssl cipi api token create New app PHP versions must be 8.3 , 8.4 , 8.5 (Cipi 4.5.4+) or 8.6 (Cipi 5.9.1+ / API 1.39.2+). d: cipi/sdk for Laravel and any PHP app.
x: PHP SDK cipi/sdk is the PHP client for the Cipi panel API. From a Laravel app, a Symfony service, or a plain script, one Sanctum token calls the same REST surface as cipi-cli and the control panel : apps, deploys, domains, databases, and the server. The SDK runs on your machine. It does not SSH into the VPS and it does not shell out to cipi . The server still needs the API package. Install and enable the panel API first ( cipi api ), then create a token with cipi api token create . Grant only the abilities this application needs. Install composer require cipi/sdk Requires PHP 8.2+ with ext-cur
